To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) recurrent networks trained to memorize input are arbitrarily bad at prediction, and (2) one-node recurrent networks optimized for prediction have predictive performance that is nearly as good as five-node recurrent networks optimized to predict.
(1) recurrent networks optimized for memory are not good at prediction and (2) recurrent networks optimized to be predictive are as good as randomly generated networks of five times as many nodes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the relationship between memory and prediction and the effect of training recurrent networks on their ability to predict.
the relationship between the ability of a recurrent network to memorize its input and its ability to predict the next value in the sequence.
understanding and optimizing reservoirs of recurrent neural networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the difference between prediction and memory is that prediction is a function of input and memory is a function of the network itself.
recurrent neural networks optimized for predictive performance are not necessarily optimized for memory performance and that the two optimization criteria are in fact orthogonal.
the memory of a network can be increased without affecting the predictive ability, and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the memory and prediction are two distinct and different problems.
we show the difference between memory and predictability in a recurrent network and that the best predictor is a single Wiener filter.
the memory capacity of a network is not a good indicator of its ability to make predictions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability of recurrent networks to predict is fundamentally limited by the number of parameters they can use to represent a function.
the goal of prediction is not the same as the goal of memorization, and that the two should not be conflated.
recurrent neural network reservoirs can be designed for prediction and that such networks can be very small.
